claims: Artemis II is carrying four astronauts on a 10-day mission to fly around the Moon and return to Earth.
Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
The Artemis II crew will test the Orion spacecraft's systems in deep space.
The Artemis II crew will swing around the far side of the Moon before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean.
The destination of the Artemis II mission is a lunar flyby orbiting the Moon rather than landing.
The crew of Artemis II consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II mission includes a high-speed return.
The Artemis II mission tests the spacecraft's life support systems.
The Artemis II crew is expected to travel farther into space than any human in history.
The Artemis II mission potentially surpasses the distance record set by Apollo 13.
Artemis II is designed to verify that the Orion capsule and Space Launch System (SLS) rocket can safely transport humans to deep space and return them to Earth.
